title: Implement runtime ABI fingerprinting and dependency shrinkwrap for GPU hosts
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Upgrades to CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS have caused intermittent startup failures and unpredictable fallback behavior on heterogeneous GPU fleets. Root cause analysis shows nondeterministic symbol resolution + implicit transitive .so dependencies and subtle ABI mismatches across kernel bundles. Existing heuristics detect failures only after runtime faults, increasing incident MTTI and complicating rollbacks.

Goal: Provide a deterministic, low-cost way to surface ABI/dep mismatches before executing production workloads by (1) computing a stable runtime ABI fingerprint for each host + kernel bundle, and (2) introducing a shrinkwrap lockfile (gpu-shrinkwrap.lock) that explicitly pins the minimal dynamic library graph we expect at startup. The fingerprinting verifier will gate model-serving processes with a configurable soft/hard policy and emit structured telemetry for automated rollbacks and canary decisions.

Non-goals: This ticket does NOT implement full binary grafting or live in-place kernel replacement. It focuses on detection, explicit lockfiles, and safe-fallback policies that integrate with existing rollout automation.
design_notes: Fingerprint: sha256 over ordered list: build-id of runtime binary, exported symbol names + version tags (where present), package metadata (CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA package version strings), and permissive hardware capability bitmap. Store as hex string in /etc/redwood/gpu-abi-fingerprint.

Shrinkwrap: gpu-shrinkwrap.lock lists absolute sonames (libcutlass.so.3 => libcutlass.so.3.7.1), minimal transitive closures discovered by static ldd-like analysis during CI image build, and a short rationale field for each pinned dep.

Verifier runtime: lightweight C++ agent (integrated into runtime bootstrap) that compares host fingerprint against model bundle fingerprint and shrinkwrap expectations. Two modes: soft (warn + allow) and hard (reject/start fallback).
Telemetry: structured events to observability (Console rollout dashboard) with fields: host_fingerprint, bundle_fingerprint, mismatch_reason, chosen_policy, fallback_taken, candidate_rollback_id.
Integration: tie verifier decisions into the Canary/rollout control plane so automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or capacity tier can occur without human intervention.
Migration: initially enable in canary clusters only. Gradually expand by adding opt-in annotate to Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: CI job generates gpu-shrinkwrap.lock for each base runtime image and uploads to artifact storage
Runtime agent computes host fingerprint within 200ms of startup and publishes to /var/run/redwood/abi.json
Console shows mismatch telemetry for at least one intentionally-misaligned canary (test harness) and triggers automated fallback according to soft policy
No measurable increase in median cold-start beyond 5% for measured canaries (p95 cold-start < baseline + 5%)
Security review sign-off on fingerprinting artifact storage and lockfile integrity checks
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (CI + lockfile): Add job to image-build pipeline that runs symbol-extractor + transitive-ldd analysis to produce gpu-shrinkwrap.lock and artifact metadata. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/ABI+Fingerprinting+Spec
Phase 2 (runtime verifier): Ship lightweight verifier as part of runtime v1.20; default mode=soft for non-dedicated clusters. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621
Phase 3 (observability + rollout hooks): Emit structured telemetry and hook verifier outcomes into rollout controller. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/198
Phase 4 (canary expansion): Enable hard mode for selected dedicated pools after 2 weeks of soft-mode stability
Phase 5 (policy automation): Add auto-rollback and model-variant fallback rules tied to mismatch signals
test_plan: Unit: symbol extractor tests with synthetic .so bundles (expected fingerprints)
Integration: CI image job produces shrinkwrap and job validates deterministic idempotency across repeated builds
Chaos: introduce a seeded ABI mismatch in a canary cluster and assert telemetry + fallback triggers
Performance: benchmark cold-start timer with and without verifier across 50 canary instances
risks_and_mitigation: False-positives due to nondeterministic symbol ordering: mitigate by canonical sorting in fingerprint pipeline and tagging tolerant symbols in shrinkwrap
Lockfile drift between builds: add automatic diff alerting in image-promotion flow and require human approval for shrinkwrap changes
Operational impact of hard rejections: start in soft mode and use canary gates before global rollout
Security: attacker could attempt to spoof fingerprint on compromised hosts; mitigate by storing signed fingerprints in artifact registry and validating signatures at bootstrap
rollout_plan: Week 1: enable CI generation and store artifacts behind signed registry
Week 2-3: deploy verifier to canaries (soft mode) + add telemetry dashboards
Week 4: enable hard mode on 2 dedicated test pools if no regressions
Week 6: full Dedicated rollout with automated rollback policies and operator playbook
notes: Related tickets: ENG-962540 (symbol-namespace isolation), ENG-271450 (gpu dep orchestration).
